component: A toggle reports what is shown, not what is wanted (Board toggle pressed over an empty column)
explanation:
CaissaTrainer Phase 2 (notes-app.md A9). Observed: an unlabelled icon toggle showed pressed while no board was on screen, because the content width left of the rail (916px) was under the 1000px the board needs. Fix: labelled Board button, aria-pressed means shown, and when the viewport allows a board but the width does not the button is disabled with its reason (Close Notebooks to make room for the board). Proposed: pressed follows the visible state; an unavailable toggle is disabled with a reason, never styled as on. Same principle applies to the workspace panel toggles, where aria-pressed is true while the panel is docked or its drawer is open. No approved rule covers toggle state honesty.

PHASE 3 UPDATE (2026-10-29, claude-agent, draft text only): panel toggles no longer use aria-pressed. A control that shows or hides a region reports aria-expanded (is the region on screen), which is the honest state the draft asked for; the edge chevron and the stacked disclosure row use it (FB-0037). An unavailable panel has no control at all instead of a disabled one (FB-0041: a module that does not offer notes renders no chevron). The 'Board' toggle on the notes board stays a labelled disclosure ('Show board' / 'Hide board', aria-expanded, aria-controls).

classification.rationale: No rule on pressed state versus visible state or on disabled with a reason. Gap, small. Owner confirmation needed.
